scenario_prompt: Write a two-paragraph executive summary addressed directly to a fictional buyer's Chief Financial Officer, recommending a cloud migration. Context: a mid-market freight brokerage firm is moving its load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances) running on Hyper-V (620 virtual machines) onto Google Cloud, targeting Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, over a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme. The CFO has stated she is measured on reducing the current $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit, which opens in 6 months. Cover why this matters to her now and what she should expect from the programme. Return only the summary text, two paragraphs, no headers.
text:
Executive summary

You state you are measured on cutting the $1,850,000 annual technology spend you carry today and on a clean DOT compliance audit that opens in six months. Right now that spend runs 28 Microsoft SQL Server instances across 620 Hyper-V virtual machines, supporting load-matching and carrier-settlement — the two systems a DOT auditor will examine most closely. This proposal replaces that on-premises SQL Server/Hyper-V estate with Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, over a 24-month, $4,200,000 programme, so the estate you answer for at audit time is the one you are actively simplifying, not the one you are defending as-is.

You should expect the programme to run against your two named priorities, not as an architecture exercise: [MC-1 GAP: current $1,850,000 spend has no stated per-instance or per-VM baseline, so the run-rate reduction this migration is expected to produce cannot yet be quantified] and [MC-16 GAP: no submission date, review checklist, or named DOT audit criteria have been supplied, so the six-month audit-readiness milestones cannot be sequenced against the programme's 24-month timeline]. What is fixed is the shift itself: today, 28 SQL Server instances on Hyper-V; after the programme, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL on Compute Engine. Before this document is sent, both gaps need your input — the current spend broken out by instance/VM, and the audit's own review dates — so the business case in front of you carries figures you have verified rather than ones this document estimated.

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| [MC-1 GAP] | MC-1 | Baseline breakdown of the $1,850,000 spend by instance/VM, so the reduction this migration produces can be stated as a figure rather than a direction |
| [MC-16 GAP] | MC-16 | The DOT audit's own review dates, scope, and criteria, so programme milestones can be sequenced against the six-month window |
